name: CM Spine (Zeng et al., Electronics 2024): 208 intraoperative lumbar G-arm images
what: 208 anteroposterior lumbar spine images at 1024 x 1024, taken during surgery with a mobile dual-mode G-arm (Geelin500-A), of patients with lumbar disc herniation or vertebral compression fractures, each lumbar vertebra in view annotated by its level, L1 to L5, 537 vertebrae, split 148 and 60 in the paper (Zeng et al., Electronics 2024;13(11):2137); the paper's data statement points to its repository, which links this Drive file as the set; the data platform's download of the file came back empty, so what it holds now is not checked
level_truth: each lumbar vertebra's level, L1 to L5, as the authors annotated it
licence: none stated: the paper's data statement and its repository's README name no licence, and the repository has no licence file (read 2026-10-23)
how_to_get: Open https://drive.google.com/file/d/1r9wX1802gkU4-EQHMMlyAlEiWXGWLhhJ/view logged in to the owner's Google account and see whether it still holds the 208 images, since the data platform's gdown got an empty download; the paper's repository, https://github.com/zengyuyuyu/Neighbor, links it as the set.

No licence is stated, so the owner decides whether to take the set as it is or to write to the corresponding author, Bo Song, for terms first; the fetch is then a Slurm job on the owner's word, never on the login node.

The route as the manifest prints it: python3 data/reproduce/reacquire/reacquire.py --grid cm_spine_drive_file; on the grid, from ~/spinesurg-ct-nnunet/data_platform/reacquire, sbatch -D "$PWD" --export=ALL,IDS="cm_spine_drive_file",MODE=--run reacquire.sbatch, as a Slurm job on the owner's word.
